scx.title: Scheduler
scx.hint: The sched_ext scheduler that runs while you play. The scx_loader service starts and stops it.
scx.noKernel: This kernel does not have sched_ext, so there is no scheduler to choose here.
scx.noService: The kernel has sched_ext, but the scx_loader service is not installed.
scx.aboutNone: No scheduler of sched_ext: the kernel uses its own.
scx.aboutUnknown: A scheduler this panel has no description of.

about.scx_beerland: Keeps each task close to the core it ran on and scales to many cores. For cache-heavy work and machines with many processors.
about.scx_bpfland: Puts interactive tasks first. For games, streaming and audio, above all with heavy work running in the background.
about.scx_cake: Built for gaming responsiveness and general use: tasks wait as little as possible while the caches stay warm.
about.scx_chaos: Adds delays on purpose to expose timing bugs in programs. It makes the machine slower: only for testing.
about.scx_cosmos: Light and general purpose: keeps each task on the same core while the machine is not saturated. Desktop or server.
about.scx_eevdf: The kernel's own scheduler (EEVDF) brought to sched_ext. Experimental, for comparing.
about.scx_flash: Fair and predictable, ordered by deadline. For work that needs low latency, such as multimedia or real-time audio.
about.scx_flow: Experimental: orders tasks by deadline and virtual time. For low latency applications and the desktop.
about.scx_forge: A base meant to be tuned by its own optimizer, scx-forge-agent. As it comes, a general scheduler.
about.scx_lavd: Measures how sensitive to delay each task is. Made for games: more fluid and fewer stutters.
about.scx_layered: Very configurable: splits tasks into layers with their own rules. It needs a configuration written for the machine.
about.scx_mavd: Experimental variant of scx_lavd with the same goal: games without stutters.
about.scx_mitosis: Isolates groups of programs into cells with their own cores. Made for servers.
about.scx_mlfq: Experimental: three queues, for interactive tasks, the rest and the heavy ones. For games and the desktop with work in the background.
about.scx_nitosis: Experimental version of scx_mitosis. It needs a newer kernel than the current ones.
about.scx_p2dq: General purpose: spreads the load across the caches of the processor, picking the less busy of two places.
about.scx_pandemonium: Adapts every decision in real time to a latency limit it measures, with no classes of tasks. Aims at quick answers under load.
about.scx_rlfifo: A simple round robin, as a template for tests. Not for everyday use.
about.scx_rustland: Its policy runs as a normal program, in Rust. Puts interactive tasks first: games, video calls, streaming.
about.scx_rusty: Balances the load between domains of the processor and can be tuned for any machine or workload.
about.scx_tickless: For servers, virtual machines and computing: removes noise of the system from most cores. Not for games.

gamemode.title: GameMode
gamemode.subtitle: Governor of the kernel and the graphics card while you play.
gamemode.serviceOff: The game mode service is stopped.
gamemode.serviceOffHint: Without it the system settings cannot be changed.
gamemode.viewHint: Choose how much you want to see. The basic view is enough to play.
gamemode.onText: Ready. Everything goes back to normal when you close the game.
gamemode.pendingText: Some pieces are missing for the game mode to give its best.

kernel.title: Kernels on this machine
kernel.hint: The ones installed and which one is in use. Installing or changing the one that boots is Kernel Installer's job.
kernel.plainHint: The game mode works with this kernel, but the new scheduler needs another one that brings it.

gamemode.effect: While you play it raises the processor frequency, takes the graphics to the top and clears the disk. When the game closes, everything goes back to how it was.
gamemode.unitMissing: This installation does not include the game mode service: it comes in the .deb package.
gamemode.gameModeText: GameMode daemon of the system: gives the game priority and keeps the screen saver away. It can be used together with the profiles.
gamemode.automaticText: Applies the profile by itself and undoes it when the game closes.
gamemode.excludedHint: Press to take it into account again
gamemode.applyError: The profile could not be applied
gamemode.strongText: Everything at its limit while you play.
gamemode.coolText: Less heat and less fan, giving up some performance.
gamemode.iniSystem: There is also a /etc/gamemode.ini of the system. The panel leaves it alone: it writes yours, which is read after it.

profile.maxText: Everything at the limit: high frequency, graphics at full and the disk cleared for the game.
profile.balancedText: Good in the game without burning power or heat.
profile.quietText: For laptops: less heat and less fan, giving up some performance.
